Topics · Who was Muhammad?

What does Muhammad's life before 40 tell us?

The Quran says Muhammad lived among his people a lifetime, then asks: will you not reason? What does it show?

Part 1 of 4

﴿قُل لَّوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَآ أَدْرَىٰكُم بِهِۦ ۖ فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا مِّن قَبْلِهِۦٓ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "If Allāh had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it.[516] Then will you not reason?"

Translator's notes

[516] The Prophet (ﷺ) lived among his people forty years before receiving any revelation.

Quran · Yunus 10:16

The verse gives the Prophet one line to say to those who doubted him: I stayed among you a lifetime before this, so will you not reason? The argument is short. It is hard to hide what you are from a small town across a lifetime. Had he been known for tales, books and great claims, they would have known. The verse asks them only to consult their own memory. The evidence it calls on belongs to them, and not to him.

A question for you

If you had known someone all their life and they suddenly spoke like this, what would you look at first?

If you sayWhether they had ever lied.
ThenThe next part takes that up.
If you sayWhether they had been studying in secret.
ThenThat was suspected in his time, the Quran records it, and it has its own Step.
If you sayWhether something had happened to their mind.
ThenThe Quran asks that itself, and invites people to think it over one by one.

Part 2 of 4

﴿مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَىٰ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Your companion [i.e., Muḥammad] has not strayed, nor has he erred,

Quran · An-Najm 53:2

﴿وَمَا صَاحِبُكُم بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And your companion [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) ] is not [at all] mad.[1871]

Translator's notes

[1871] Literally, "possessed by jinn."

Quran · At-Takwir 81:22

The Quran has a particular word for him when it speaks to his opponents: your companion. Your companion has not strayed. Your companion is not mad. It is an unusual word for a dispute. It does not say this stranger or this new teacher. It says the one you know, the one you walked beside. Each time it sends them back to what they knew. After his call they named him a sorcerer and a liar, and the Quran records that too, yet it asks them about the life before.

A question for you

If his people knew him as honest before the claim, what would that show?

If you sayThat he told the truth in his claim.
ThenIt shows that lying is not the nearest explanation. The chance of honest error remains, and the next part comes closer.
If you sayOnly that he was sincere.
ThenThat is the exact limit, and many historians say as much. Sincerity alone does not settle it, which is why the strands accumulate.
If you sayNot very much.
ThenThen you will not lean on it alone, which is wise. Set it with the others.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَرْجُوٓا۟ أَن يُلْقَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبُ إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۖ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْكَـٰفِرِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And you were not expecting that the Book would be conveyed to you, but [it is] a mercy from your Lord. So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.[1121]

Translator's notes

[1121] In their religion by making any concessions to their beliefs.

Quran · Al-Qasas 28:86

Someone planning a claim prepares for it. The verse says something else of the Prophet: you had no hope that the Book would be given to you, except as mercy from your Lord. That is the Quran's statement, and it cannot be proved or disproved from outside. But consider what can be examined: a long life with no report of a claim to prophecy, then recitation that continued for over twenty years. That is what needs explaining: not only what came, but this turn, and this endurance.

A question for you

What do you think explains a quiet life followed by all this?

If you sayHe spent those years listening and thinking.
ThenA serious reply. Then the question moves to what he could have heard, and whether it would be enough.
If you saySomething changed within him.
ThenPeople do change. Then ask what changed him, and whether that explains what he brought.
If you saySomething reached him from beyond himself.
ThenThat is the Quran's own account. The next part asks what it cost him.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ مَالِ هَـٰذَا ٱلرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشِى فِى ٱلْأَسْوَاقِ ۙ لَوْلَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُۥ نَذِيرًا٧ أَوْ يُلْقَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ كَنزٌ أَوْ تَكُونُ لَهُۥ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا ۚ وَقَالَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَّسْحُورًا٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why was there not sent down to him an angel so he would be with him a warner? Or [why is not] a treasure presented to him [from heaven], or does he [not] have a garden from which he eats?" And the wrongdoers say, "You follow not but a man affected by magic."

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:7-8

﴿قُلْ مَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ أَن يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ سَبِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "I do not ask of you for it any payment - only that whoever wills might take to his Lord a way."

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:57

Translation

I coveted no one’s silver, gold, or clothing. You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.

Original · Ancient Greek

ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα· αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσι μετʼ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται.

Acts · 20:33-34

World English Bible

What did the claim bring him? The Quran keeps his opponents' words: why does this messenger eat food and walk in the markets? Where is his treasure? The one they describe has no treasure and no throne. The Quran has him say: I ask you no wage. It speaks of his chest tightening at what they said. He later came to lead a community, and that should be said plainly. But those years in his city were years of endurance.

A question for you

What do these years add to your scale?

If you sayThey speak for his sincerity.
ThenThat is what endurance usually speaks for. Add it to the rest, then ask about the source.
If you sayLeaders can live simply too.
ThenTrue, and no single strand is enough. See how the Quran speaks to the Prophet himself.
If you sayI want to hear about the teacher.
ThenThat is the next strand.

Your reflection

If someone asked those who have lived beside you for years, what would you hope they could say?
